items.title: Derivation of third Equation of Motion by Graphical method

blocks.text: This is the third equation of motion.

The equations of motion are useful in solving the problems relating to linear motion with uniform acceleration, when an object moves along a straight line. If its direction of motion does not change, then all the vector quantities can be manipulated like scalars. In such cases initial velocity is taken as positive. A negative sign is assigned to quantities where direction is opposite to that of initial velocity. In the absence of air resistance, all objects in free fall at the surface of the Earth, move toward the Earth with a uniform acceleration. This acceleration is known as acceleration due to gravity, denoted by g and its average value at the Earth surface is taken as 9.8 ms⁻² in the downward direction. The equation for uniformally accelerated motion can also be applied to free fall motion of the object by replacing a by g.

blocks.title: Example 2.2
blocks.problem: A car travelling at 10 m s⁻¹ accelerates uniformally at 2 m s⁻². Calculate its velocity after 5 s.
steps:
vi = 10 m s⁻¹
a = 2 m s⁻²
t = 5 s
vf = ?

using first equation of motion, we can write
vf = vi + at
vf = 10 m s⁻¹ + 2 m s⁻² × 5 s

blocks.title: Example 2.3
blocks.problem: A car travels with initial velocity of 15 m s⁻¹. It accelerates at a rate of 2 m s⁻² for 4 seconds. Find the displacement of the car.
steps:
Given that
vi = 15 m s⁻¹
a = 2 m s⁻²
t = 4 s
Displacement S = ?

By using 2nd equation of motion
S = vit + ½at²

Putting the values
S = (15 m s⁻¹ × 4 s) + ½(2 m s⁻²)(16 s)²

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: In the substitution the book prints (16 s)²; it should be (4 s)² = 16 s². The book's answer uses 16 s²: S = 60 m + ½ × 2 m s⁻² × 16 s² = 60 m + 16 m = 76 m, which is right.

blocks.title: Example 2.4
blocks.problem: In a short distance race, a contestant in a car starts from rest and reaches velocity of 300 km h⁻¹, after covering a distance of 0.45 km at a constant acceleration. Find this constant acceleration.
steps:
Initial velocity = vi = 0
Final velocity = vf = 300 km h⁻¹
Distance covered = S = 0.45 km = 0.45 × 1000 m = 450 m

Initial velocity = vi = 0
Final velocity = vf = 300 kmh⁻¹
= (300×1000×250)/(60×60) m s⁻¹

Using third equation of motion, we have
vf² - vi² = 2as

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The repeated line prints vf = (300×1000×250)/(60×60) m s⁻¹, which would be about 20 833 m s⁻¹. The conversion is (300×1000)/(60×60) m s⁻¹ = 250/3 m s⁻¹ ≈ 83.3 m s⁻¹, as in the second line; the working that follows uses 250/3 m s⁻¹ and its answer 7.72 m s⁻² is right.
